  "title": "Prompt users to accept again if they haven't consented to the TOS or the TOS has been updated.",
  "body": "We need a mechanism to ask existing users to consent to the TOS if we don't have data that they've done so at checkout. This could be because they were added manually or joined the site before the recent TOS updates went out.

We also want to ask users to consent again if the TOS has been updated. Maybe we should just check for changes to the TOS page or maybe we should allow admins to kick this off.

WordPress core has been working on similar features. Here is one related ticket: https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/44043

If we can, we should piggy back on the systems and style/UI/etc that core is using for this.",

      "body": "> Maybe we should allow admins to kick this off.

Yes.

> Maybe we should just check for changes to the TOS page

No. Because TOS page can be an embed of an external TOS content by 3rd party generators like Iubenda.
Also, If I spot a typo or I want to rephrase a paragraph, doesn't always require to reaccept the TOS.

---

RE Consent API, some more history:

https://wpconsentapi.org/
This is an interesting demo of the Consent API framework from the WP Privacy Team.
- https://wordpress.org/plugins/wp-consent-api/
- https://github.com/rlankhorst/wp-consent-level-api/

At the time of writing it's integrated with:
- Cookiebot
- Compliantz.io
- An example plugin: https://github.com/rlankhorst/consent-api-example-plugin

The official feature proposal https://make.wordpress.org/core/2020/04/01/feature-plugin-proposal-wp-consent-api/

Compliantz has an article about how they are using the Consent API to avoid issues with CF7 integration: https://complianz.io/why-the-wp-consent-api-is-important-a-case-study-with-cf7-and-recaptcha/

      "url": "https://github.com/strangerstudios/paid-memberships-pro/issues/723#issuecomment-6062457575",
      "created_at": "2026-10-08T14:47:23Z",

      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Consolidating #3633 into this issue, since this one is older. Context carried over from there:

**Proposal from #3633** (@kimwhite, April 2026)
- PMPro already logs TOS consent in user meta (`pmpro_consent_log`), including the TOS page's `post_modified` at the time of consent, and `pmpro_is_consent_current()` can tell when the TOS page has changed since. What's missing is a way to surface that to members and prompt them to re-accept.
- Proposed: an admin trigger ("Require all members to re-accept this Terms of Service" when editing the TOS page), a modal or interstitial for members with stale or missing consent that doesn't require a new payment, and logging the acceptance the same way checkout does.
- WordPress core added a privacy policy update flow but never shipped the "force re-check" piece, so PMPro would need its own.
- Workaround for free levels: redirect active members with stale or missing consent to checkout with their current level. That isn't acceptable for paid levels.
- It would be worth getting input from affected customers on the ideal UX before building.

**Scoping after PR #3800** (closed)
We still want this, but #3800 showed there are decisions to make before it can be built:
- **Mechanism:** a banner can be ignored indefinitely. A redirect on login misses members with persistent sessions and collides with the existing login redirect filters. A content gate is the only option that guarantees acceptance, and the only one that can lock a paying member out.
- **Who is prompted:** active members only? Expired members who still have an account? Users with admin-assigned or imported levels who never saw a TOS at checkout? Administrators?
- **Where the setting lives:** a checkbox on the TOS page edit screen, or a standing policy next to the existing TOS setting in Advanced Settings.
- **What counts as a new version:** consent currency is an exact match on the page's modified date, so every save of the TOS page, including a typo fix, would re-prompt everyone. That lines up with @mircobabini's point above that admins should trigger re-acceptance rather than every edit.
- **Non-browser access:** the REST API and any app-based access need a defined behavior under whichever mechanism we pick.

Full original thread: #3633
"
